extracted.intended_audience: prospective readers/subscribers, advertisers, and potential contributors to The Forerunner (readers interested in women’s issues and social reform)
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial statement and publishing guidelines for The Forerunner: its mission, scope of contents, advertising policy, departmental boundaries, authorship, and subscriber value proposition. Intended to define what material the magazine will publish and how advertising will be handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magazine format and authorship (What is The Forerunner?)
rubrics_metrics.description: _What is The Forerunner?_  It is a monthly magazine, publishing stories short and serial, article and essay; drama, verse, satire and sermon; dialogue, fable and fantasy, comment and review.  It is written entirely by Charlotte Perkins Gilman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the magazine as a monthly, single-author publication covering many literary forms (short stories, serials, essays, drama, verse, satire, sermon, dialogue, fable, fantasy, comment, review). Emphasizes single-author voice and consistent authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission / purpose (What is it For?)
rubrics_metrics.description: _What is it For?_  It is to stimulate thought: to arouse hope, courage and impatience; to offer practical suggestions and solutions, to voice the strong assurance of better living, here, now, in our own hands to make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial criterion: material should stimulate thought, inspire hope/courage/constructive impatience, offer practical solutions, and promote immediatist, practical betterment of life. Tone expected: purposeful, instructive, and encouraging reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject focus and viewpoint (What is it about?)
rubrics_metrics.description: _What is it about?_  It is about people, principles, and the questions of every-day life; the personal and public problems of to-day.  It gives a clear, consistent view of human life and how to live it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content must address everyday personal and public problems, combine human interest with principled analysis, and present a clear, consistent perspective on living. Prefer pieces that blend practical counsel with overarching principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of genders and children (Is it a Woman's magazine?)
rubrics_metrics.description: _Is it a Woman's magazine?_  It will treat all three phases of our existence--male, female and human.  It will discuss Man, in his true place in life; Woman, the Unknown Power; the Child, the most important citizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial expectation: inclusive treatment of male, female, and general human subjects; special attention to the role and potential of women and to the importance of children. Not restricted to 'women's interests' narrowly—aims at broad human concerns with emphasis on woman and child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political/social stance (Is it a Socialist Magazine?)
rubrics_metrics.description: _Is it a Socialist Magazine?_  It is a magazine for humanity, and humanity is social.  It holds that Socialism, the economic theory, is part of our gradual Socialization, and that the duty of conscious humanity is to promote Socialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets an interpretive stance: accepts socialization/socialism as relevant explanatory/prescriptive framework. Contributors and content should be compatible with a humane/social perspective and sympathetic to social reform and socialization themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising policy (As to Advertising)
rubrics_metrics.description: We have long heard that "A pleased customer is the best advertiser." The Forerunner offers to its advertisers and readers the benefit of this authority. In its advertising department, under the above heading, will be described articles personally known and used. So far as individual experience and approval carry weight, and clear truthful description command attention, the advertising pages of The Forerunner will be useful to both dealer and buyer. If advertisers prefer to use their own statements The Forerunner will publish them if it believes them to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising should be based on personal knowledge/experience and truthful description. The magazine will publish advertisers' own statements only if the editors believe them true. Emphasizes honest, experience-based testimonials rather than exaggerated claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content plan and featured departments (As to Contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: The main feature of the first year is a new book on a new subject with a new name: "Our Androcentric Culture." ... "What Diantha Did." this is a serial novel. ... Among the short articles will appear: "Private Morality and Public Immorality." "The Beauty Women Have Lost" "Our Overworked Instincts." "The Nun in the Kitchen." "Genius: Domestic and Maternal." ... There will be short stories and other entertaining matter in each issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides specific planned regular features (a new book, serial novel, numerous short articles on social/domestic topics, stories, poems, sermons, commentary). Use list of suggested topics as editorial themes. Submissions should align with these thematic areas: domestic life, social critique, women's roles, child-rearing, economics/ethics/civics, arts and crafts, literature, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal Problems department scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The department of "Personal Problems" does not discuss etiquette, fashions or the removal of freckles. Foolish questions will not be answered, unless at peril of the asker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline for the advice column: avoid trivial/banal topics (etiquette, fashions, cosmetic trivialities). Prefer serious, substantive personal and social problem questions; editors reserve the right to refuse to answer foolish queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriber value proposition (As to Value)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you take this magazine one year you will have: One complete novel . . . By C. P. Gilman; One new book . . . By C. P. Gilman; Twelve short stories . . . By C. P. Gilman; Twelve-and-more short articles . . . By C. P. Gilman; Twelve-and-more new poems . . . By C. P. Gilman; Twelve Short Sermons . . . By C. P. Gilman; Besides "Comment and Review" . . . By C. P. Gilman; "Personal Problems" . . . By C. P. Gilman. DON'T YOU THINK IT'S WORTH A DOLLAR?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets concrete editorial deliverables and pricing (quantity and types of material per year) to justify subscription cost. Useful as a standard for planning issue content and for marketing/subscription messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship / editorial control
rubrics_metrics.description: It is written entirely by Charlotte Perkins Gilman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declares single-author control — content, editorial voice, and policy are centralized. Contributors and advertisers must conform to the editor/author's standards and viewpoints; no open contributor pool is implied.
